rules.cwe_name: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments
rules.description: A string formatting operation, such as '"%s: %s, %s" % (a,b)', where the number of conversion specifiers in the format string differs from the number of values to be formatted will raise a TypeError.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Request/Response Splitting')
rules.description: Writing user input directly to an HTTP header makes code vulnerable to attack by header splitting.

rules.cwe_name: Observable Timing Discrepancy
rules.description: When checking a Hash over a message, a constant-time algorithm should be used. Otherwise, an attacker may be able to forge a valid Hash for an arbitrary message by running a timing attack if they can send to the validation procedure. A successful attack can result in authentication bypass.

rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
rules.description: Binding a socket to all interfaces opens it up to traffic from any IPv4 address and is therefore associated with security risks.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component ('Injection')
rules.description: user provided command can lead to execute code on a external server that can be belong to other users or admins

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File
rules.description: From user-controlled data saved in CSV files, it is easy to attempt information disclosure or other malicious activities when automated by spreadsheet software

rules.cwe_name: Direct Request ('Forced Browsing')
rules.description: A restricted route, URL, script, or file can be requested directly without required authorization.

rules.cwe_name: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
rules.description: Cookies without the `HttpOnly` attribute set can be accessed by JS scripts, making them more vulnerable to XSS attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')
rules.description: Untrusted CR or LF characters are not neutralized before use in line-delimited protocol metadata.
